audit_findings.title: Post-close MicroAge economics are absent from both the numerator and financing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $220.5 million purchase price, equal to 18.1% of the $1.218 billion base equity value; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: MicroAge owner earnings, integration and purchase-accounting costs, and incremental borrowing interest are absent from OE, while post-close cash and financing are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: ScanSource expects to fund the acquisition through borrowings under its existing credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter-date error if the supplied September 1 closing record is controlling: the September 6 valuation describes the pre-close business despite its own September 1 rerun trigger. The omitted transaction is large enough to change the conclusion, but direction cannot be determined because acquired earnings add value while interest, integration costs, purchase accounting and any cash use reduce it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing statement, purchase-price allocation, acquisition borrowing amount and rate, post-close cash balance, MicroAge normalized earnings and integration costs; then rerun OE and the bridge on one consistent post-close perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.150 million, or $1.32 per diluted share and 2.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The contingent-payment liability is a claim ahead of common equity that would reduce the equity bridge unless its burden is already fully captured in OE
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recorded contingent consideration liabilities for Advantix, Resourcive, and DataXoom.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, although the correct adjustment remains conditional on avoiding double counting with the $1.073 million remeasurement expense. A full $28.150 million deduction would reduce base value from $57.03 to approximately $55.71 per share and buy-below from $39.92 to approximately $39.00. That does not reverse the existing conclusion at the $58.48 market price and is small relative to the $48.92-$63.20 scenario range.
audit_findings.action: Trace whether the $1.073 million remeasurement expense was retained in OE, obtain the earnout payment schedule and expected cash amounts, and rerun the bridge with the liability deducted or its economic payment burden modeled without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Purged interest income may include operating customer-finance income
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified customer-finance portion of the $12.264 million pre-tax caption; full-caption upper bound is $9.321 million after tax and approximately $6.13 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: Improperly purged operating interest would understate anchor OE and every forecast and terminal-period cash flow while leaving the associated customer receivables in operating capital
audit_findings.evidence: Interest income for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 increased compared to the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025 primarily from increased interest income on cash balances and customer receivables.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the caption contains both cash-balance and customer-receivable income, but it does not provide the split. Thus the classification problem is demonstrated while its actual magnitude is unresolved. If a meaningful portion is operating income, restoring it could change the base comparison with the $58.48 market price; the record cannot establish whether that threshold is reached.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the general-ledger or note-level split of FY2026 interest income between cash investments, trade receivables and advisor-financing notes; retain the operating portion, purge only income associated with separately added cash, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Supplier concentration threatens the durability assumed by the terminal value
audit_findings.magnitude: Cisco and Zebra each exceed 10% of sales, together exceeding 20%; terminal value represents 47.7%-50.9% of scenario value
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss or adverse repricing of supplier relationships could reduce revenue, rebates and margins, increase working-capital needs, and invalidate projected growth and terminal durability
audit_findings.evidence: The Company sells products from many suppliers; however, sales of products supplied by Cisco and Zebra each constituted more than 10 % of the Company's net sales for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration and short termination periods are filed facts, but no actual termination or adverse term change is supplied. This is therefore a forward-looking durability risk rather than a demonstrated numerical error. Its dollar effect is unquantified because vendor-level gross profit, rebates and replacement economics are not disclosed.
audit_findings.action: Monitor Cisco and Zebra renewals and obtain vendor-level sales, gross profit, rebate dependence and working-capital data; rerun growth, margins and terminal assumptions if either relationship or its economics deteriorates.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may retain a nonrecurring cyber-insurance recovery
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.838 million pre-tax and $0.629 million after tax; maximum modeled effect is approximately $0.35-$0.46 per share across the scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the one-time recovery inflates anchor OE and is capitalized through forecast and terminal cash flows
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company received $ 0.8 million and $ 5.9 million, respectively, of insurance proceeds from claims filed related to the cybersecurity attack.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the recovery remains in the $80.4 million anchor is unresolved, so this is not a demonstrated calculation error. Even assuming full inclusion, the filed $0.629 million after-tax amount is only 0.8% of anchor OE and would reduce modeled values by approximately $0.35, $0.41 and $0.46 per share in the bear, base and bull cases, respectively—insufficient to change the valuation conclusion or the margin-of-safety decision.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $0.838 million recovery through the FY2026 OE reconciliation and, if retained, remove the filed $0.629 million after-tax effect and refresh scenario values.
